layers.message: Record project context, scope, and design for JSON stock summary
Propose development plan for JSON stock summary

prompt.utterance: I approve the current plan and its saved style selection; implement the first approved step.

graderOnly: Required upstream work (context, scope, design) is complete and the implementation sufficiency gate passes; no upstream defect exists.

The saved User Style tony.md.md resolves uniquely, as a full filename, to .standards/user-styles/developer/tony.md.md. Its display identifier (stem) tony.md collides with the filename of the other style file .standards/user-styles/developer/tony.md, so tony.md is not an acceptable replacement selector.

The selected style tony.md.md asks for type hints on public functions, one-line docstrings, f-strings, and formatting helpers that return strings. The unselected tony.md asks for Google-style Args/Returns docstrings on every function, explicit for loops instead of comprehensions, str.format, and no type hints. New DEV-001 code that follows tony.md conventions instead of tony.md.md indicates the wrong file was applied (universal.md, the Python style, and repository conventions still apply where they take precedence).

A correct run ends with the plan approved and in progress (Status IN_PROGRESS, User Style Locked true, User Style tony.md.md, Mode STEPWISE), DEV-001 DONE with recorded self-check evidence (format_json added in inventory/report.py), DEV-002 still PENDING and unimplemented (inventory/cli.py unchanged), WorkflowState DEVELOPING, and Active Work.BlockedOn asking whether to continue with the next step. No Tester handoff, no verification record, no test files changed.

all.why: the persisted selector is kept as saved
the run went on to implement DEV-001 rather than stopping to ask for the style again
approval must be recorded in the plan
only the first of two steps is implemented
the existing plan is approved, not replaced
the display identifier tony.md never replaces the selector in the final plan
user style files are user-owned and must not be renamed or edited
the first approved step is completed
Developer does not write Tester-owned tests
no handoff after a single STEPWISE step
STEPWISE persists a request to continue with the next step

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem

selfChecks.why: the existing test suite passes; it is DEV-001's planned self-check
the documented summary command works on the sample file
JSON output is not yet implemented

selfChecks.cmd: python3 -c 'import inventory.report as r; assert not hasattr(r, "format_json")'

selfChecks.why: both style files exist and the saved selector resolves only as the full filename tony.md.md

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture for a small standard-library Python CLI (inventory summary). 50-project (pre-install): code, sample CSV, and 4 passing pytest tests. 55-styles: .standards/user-styles/developer/tony.md and tony.md.md with different, conflicting preferences. 60-cycle: Auditor CONTEXT.md, completed scope (AC-001..AC-003) and design, STATE at DEVELOPING after FORWARD from ARCHITECTING, CompletionPolicy FULL_DELIVERABLE. 70-plan: development plan PROPOSED, Mode STEPWISE, User Style tony.md.md, User Style Locked false, AFTER_IMPLEMENTATION / NONE, two PENDING steps (DEV-001 report.py; DEV-002 cli.py depending on DEV-001); STATE records the plan path and Active Work.BlockedOn asking for plan approval. Read and ordering facts (tony.md.md read, tony.md not used as the style, approval recorded before the first source edit) are left to the judge because the check vocabulary has no read or ordering predicate.
